newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan egg-hurlers mark Japan's '37 China invasion.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan egg-hurlers mark Japan's '37 China invasion.

text.p: About 20 Chinese nationalists burned a Japanese flag and hurled eggs at Japan's unofficial outpost in Taiwan on Monday, demanding that Tokyo apologise for its July 7, 1937, invasion of China.

The Taiwan activists, wielding anti-Japan banners and shouting slogans, said they wanted to deliver a protest letter, but Japanese representatives refused to come out -- triggering the angry barrage of raw eggs.
Protest organiser Ching Chieh-shou, a Taipei city councilman, said the protest aimed to "expose the intrusive character of Japanese imperialism".

A clash between Chinese and invading Japanese troops at the Marco Polo Bridge southwest of Beijing on July 7, 1937, escalated into a full-blown invasion and war that raged across China for almost a decade.

Since 1993, successive prime ministers have voiced Japan's remorse over suffering caused by its wartime aggression, but Chinese on the mainland, in Taiwan and Hong Kong continue to demand a more forthright apology -- and financial compensation.
Those voices are loudest in Taiwan, the seat since 1949 of the exiled Republic of China that took refuge on the island after being defeated by the communists on the mainland.
Tokyo recognises only Beijing and has no formal ties with Taiwan, though like most other countries it funds an unofficial Taipei mission that handles visas and other diplomatic matters.

Monday's protest followed a series of egg-tossing outbursts over the past year by Taiwan rightists angry at Tokyo's occupation of an East China Sea archipelago that is also claimed by Taipei and Beijing.

Protest leader Ching has been involved in numerous attempts to land on the archipelago, called the Diaoyus in Chinese and Senkakus in Japanese. Only one attempt succeeded, prompting Japan to intensify patrols around the uninhabited islands.
Many elderly Taiwanese can recall living under Japanese colonial rule after China's decaying Qing dynasty ceded Taiwan to Tokyo in 1895, 16 years before the Qing collapse.
The Chinese Nationalists, who toppled the Qing, retook Taiwan in 1945 after Japan's World War Two defeat.
